rows.grounds: optative expressing the power to stir or excite
compound denoting women across all cosmic realms

items.question: What power does the mantra grant to agitate women across all cosmic realms?
premises: The mantra enables agitation of targeted beings.
The targets include women of heaven, earth, and netherworld realms.
items.inference: The practitioner can stir women throughout all cosmic levels.
items.plain_english: One may agitate the women of heaven, earth, the world, and the nether regions.

rows.grounds: compound referring to all those previously mentioned

items.question: By whose agency do all those women come under the practitioner's control?
premises: The mantra practitioner acts as the agent.
All those previously mentioned become subject to control.
items.inference: Through the practitioner, all those women come under his control.
items.plain_english: O supreme goddess, by the mantra practitioner all of them come under his control.

items.question: Is there any room for doubt that the targeted person becomes subdued?
premises: The targeted person becomes subdued.
The text explicitly denies the need for doubt in this matter.
items.inference: The subjugation is certain and beyond doubt.
items.plain_english: O goddess, he becomes subdued; there should be no doubt about this.

items.question: Can this declared forcible attraction produce any outcome other than the stated one?
premises: This forcible attraction has been declared.
The text denies that it could be otherwise.
items.inference: The declared forcible attraction is unfailingly effective as stated.
items.plain_english: This has been declared as forcible attraction, and it cannot be otherwise.

rows.grounds: one whose self is burdened with great sins
one who destroys or is freed from sin

items.question: How quickly does a person burdened with great sins become freed from sin?
premises: A person may be burdened with great sins.
The practice makes one a destroyer of sin at that very moment.
items.inference: Even a greatly sinful person becomes freed from sin immediately.
items.plain_english: One burdened with great sins becomes a destroyer of sin at that very moment.

rows.grounds: compound indicating impurity accumulated over seven births

items.question: What extent of accumulated impurity can a person destroy within one month?
premises: The practice is performed over a month.
Impurity may be accumulated over seven births.
items.inference: Within a month, a person destroys impurity accumulated over seven births.
items.plain_english: In a month, a person destroys the impurity accumulated over seven births.

rows.grounds: a count of one lakh recitations
severe sins from which liberation occurs

items.question: What result follows for one who recites the mantra one hundred thousand times?
premises: A practitioner may recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
Such recitation leads to liberation from great sins.
items.inference: Reciting one hundred thousand times liberates one from great sins.
items.plain_english: Whoever recites it just one hundred thousand times is liberated from great sins.

items.question: Does the practice destroy even the foremost great sins without any doubt?
premises: The practice destroys the foremost great sins.
The text explicitly denies doubt in this matter.
items.inference: The foremost great sins are certainly destroyed.
items.plain_english: It destroys the foremost great sins; there is no doubt about this.

rows.grounds: tens of millions of great sins

items.question: Can the practice destroy even tens of millions of great sins without doubt?
premises: The practice destroys crores of great sins.
The text explicitly denies doubt in this matter.
items.inference: Even vast quantities of great sins are certainly destroyed.
items.plain_english: It destroys tens of millions of great sins; there is no doubt about this.

items.question: What status does the practitioner attain after five hundred thousand recitations?
premises: Five hundred thousand recitations are performed.
The result is compared to becoming like Kubera.
items.inference: After five hundred thousand recitations, the practitioner becomes like Kubera without doubt.
items.plain_english: O lord of gods, after five hundred thousand recitations one becomes like Kubera; there is no doubt.

rows.grounds: one who meets or joins the sky-moving beings

items.question: What attainment follows for the practitioner after seven hundred thousand recitations?
premises: The practitioner completes seven hundred thousand recitations.
This leads to association with sky-moving beings.
items.inference: After seven hundred thousand recitations, the practitioner meets the khecarīs.
uncertainties: The exact sense of khecarī+melakaḥ as meeting or union is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: After seven hundred thousand recitations, the mantra practitioner becomes one who meets the khecarīs.

items.question: Who comes under the practitioner's control, and who is especially emphasized?
premises: Kings come under the practitioner's control.
Women come under his control especially.
items.inference: Kings and especially women become subject to the practitioner.
items.plain_english: Kings and especially women come under his control.

items.question: What personal qualities and social status does the practitioner attain through this practice?
premises: The practitioner becomes honored by all.
The practitioner becomes healthy and endowed with all good fortune.
items.inference: The practice brings universal honor, health, and complete good fortune.
items.plain_english: He becomes honored by all, always healthy, and endowed with all good fortune.

items.question: What ritual must be performed diligently to obtain all accomplishments?
premises: A fire offering grants all accomplishments.
This fire offering must be performed with effort.
items.inference: A diligently performed fire offering bestows all siddhis.
items.plain_english: Then a fire offering that grants all accomplishments should be performed with effort.

items.question: What specific benefit does a fire offering performed with ghee bestow?
premises: The fire offering may be performed with ghee.
Such an offering grants mastery of speech.
items.inference: A ghee fire offering bestows mastery of speech.
items.plain_english: Performed with ghee, it also grants mastery of speech.

items.question: What result follows from six months of fire offerings combined with curd?
premises: Fire offerings are performed with curd for six months.
This practice stabilizes prosperity for the practitioner.
items.inference: Six months of curd offerings make the practitioner's prosperity stable.
items.plain_english: For six months, with offerings joined with curd, his prosperity becomes stable.

items.question: What power of control does one gain by offering ten thousand oblations?
premises: A practitioner offers ten thousand oblations.
The offering is directed to the goddess.
items.inference: Ten thousand oblations bring others under the practitioner's control.
uncertainties: The exact target of vaśaḥ is not explicitly specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: Whoever offers ten thousand oblations, O goddess, brings others under his control.

rows.grounds: a count of one lakh oblations

items.question: What lifespan does a practitioner gain by performing one hundred thousand oblations properly?
premises: One hundred thousand oblations are performed according to rule.
The practice grants extended life.
items.inference: Proper performance of one hundred thousand oblations grants a lifespan of one hundred years.
items.plain_english: By performing just one hundred thousand oblations according to rule, he may live a hundred autumns.

items.question: Is accomplishment certain for one who performs oblations counted in hundreds of thousands?
premises: A practitioner performs oblations in lakh counts.
The text denies doubt regarding the resulting accomplishment.
items.inference: Performing oblations in lakhs certainly brings accomplishment.
uncertainties: The verb governing lakṣa+saṃkhyāni is implicit from context.
items.plain_english: Whoever performs oblations in hundreds of thousands, O goddess, attains accomplishment; there is no doubt.

items.question: What attainment follows from practicing at the three daily junctures for one month?
premises: The practice is performed at the three daily junctures.
The duration is only one month.
items.inference: One month of practice at the three junctures yields mastery of speech.
items.plain_english: By practicing at the three junctures for just one month, one may obtain mastery of speech.

items.question: What level of accomplishment can the practitioner achieve through this practice?
premises: The practitioner can accomplish siddhi.
This siddhi is hard to obtain even for the gods.
items.inference: The practitioner can achieve an accomplishment rare even among the gods.
items.plain_english: The practitioner may accomplish a siddhi that is hard to obtain even for the gods.

rows.grounds: in a concealed or secret way

items.question: Under what condition does the practitioner become a treasure of knowledge?
premises: The practice must be conducted in a secret manner.
Secrecy leads to becoming a repository of knowledge.
items.inference: Only through secrecy does the practitioner become a treasure of knowledge.
items.plain_english: Only by maintaining secrecy does he become a treasure of knowledge.

items.question: Is there any exception to all beings coming under the practitioner's control?
premises: All beings come under the practitioner's control.
The text denies that it could be otherwise.
items.inference: All beings unfailingly come under the practitioner's control.
items.plain_english: All of them come under the practitioner's control, and it cannot be otherwise.

items.question: What result does a wise practitioner obtain by reciting the mantra ten thousand times?
premises: A wise practitioner recites the mantra ten thousand times.
This recitation yields a specific fruit.
items.inference: Reciting ten thousand times grants the practitioner this very fruit.
uncertainties: The specific fruit referred to by etat+eva phalaṃ depends on the immediately preceding context.
items.plain_english: O wise one, by reciting ten thousand times, one may obtain this very fruit.
